title: Nobles of Gilneas
content:
- *For other uses, see [Noble (disambiguation)](/wiki/Noble_(disambiguation)).*
The **nobles of Gilneas** are the ruling class of the [kingdom of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)). Some were slain during the [civil war](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion), while others were turned into [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) or [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) during the [Forsaken invasion](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas). Others remain [human](/wiki/Human) in exile from their homeland.[1]

## Holdings[]

The [Greymane family](/wiki/Greymane_family) rules over all of Gilneas. Their home of [Greymane Manor](/wiki/Greymane_Manor) overlooked the southern region of [Duskmist Shore](/wiki/Duskmist_Shore) and [Duskhaven](/wiki/Duskhaven), and it is located behind the [Queen's Gate](/wiki/Queen%27s_Gate) and [King's Gate](/wiki/King%27s_Gate). This area of Gilneas has since sunk outside of the manor, but once held cottages for the [Crowley](/wiki/Crowley)[2] and the Walden families.[3] [Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City) also appears to be explicitly ruled by the royal family.[1]

The [Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley) family ruled over the lands that constituted both [Pyrewood Village](/wiki/Pyrewood_Village) (and as a result, [Shadowfang Keep](/wiki/Shadowfang_Keep)) and [Ambermill](/wiki/Ambermill),[4] making [Baron Silverlaine](/wiki/Baron_Silverlaine) a vassal of theirs as a result. [Lord Mayor Morrison](/wiki/Lord_Mayor_Morrison) was also the mayor of Pyrewood, placing him implicitly under Crowley's service. [Lord Harford](/wiki/Lord_Harford) was also noted as a servant of Arugal and from beyond the wall, meaning he was likely one of Crowley's vassals as well. The [Marley](/wiki/Lord_Marley) family ruled over an unspecified province near Gilneas' borders, which at the time stretched to about the proximity of the [Deep Elem Mine](/wiki/Deep_Elem_Mine). His lands were deemed ill-suited as they lacked natural boundaries to assist with the wall. Given that his lands would not have drawn issue with the Crowleys, his territories were likely near Deep Elem Mine; perhaps [Ambermill](/wiki/Ambermill) itself and the surrounding land, which would have made him subservient to Crowley himself. Marley notably remained behind the Greymane Wall in spite of this.

The [Godfreys](/wiki/Vincent_Godfrey) ruled over a region just south of the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall), within proximity to the Northgate lands.[5] Given that Godfrey specifies the wall would cut into 'some' of Crowley's lands, and the [Northgate rebellion](/wiki/Northgate_rebellion) was named for the region that supported Crowley the most; it is unlikely that Godfrey's lands were the [Northgate Woods](/wiki/Northgate_Woods). This leaves [Emberstone Village](/wiki/Emberstone_Village) to potentially be Godfrey's holdings, which would give him ties to the eastern lords that he later convinces to betray Genn in the worgen starting zone, or the [Northern Headlands](/wiki/Northern_Headlands).

[Ashbury](/wiki/Baron_Ashbury) and [Walden](/wiki/Lord_Walden) are referred to as the "eastern lords", which would constitute areas such as [Emberstone Village](/wiki/Emberstone_Village) and [Tempest's Reach](/wiki/Tempest%27s_Reach).[6] It is not specified where either of these two lords actually rule over beside this, though the Walden family is noted to have homes outside of the east and Lord Walden himself is killed in a house in Tempest's Reach; meaning they may have been 'unlanded' nobility. [Lord Hewell](/wiki/Lord_Hewell) is also present at the meeting and spoke against turning over Genn Greymane to the Forsaken. Given the context, Hewell may also be an eastern lord, as the quest specifies that only two lords joined Godfrey's plot; alternatively he may have also been from the neighboring [Stormglen Village](/wiki/Stormglen_Village).

The lands of the [Tulvans](/wiki/Lord_Geoffery_Tulvan) and [Candrens](/wiki/Lord_Candren) are entirely unknown with no allusions to any potential regions, though the Tulvans are stated to be 'earls'. [Lord Hiram Creed](/wiki/Lord_Hiram_Creed)'s territory, if any, is also unknown. Given that he was, in truth, a drakonid, it is unknown if there is an actual Creed family that he infiltrated / impersonated into, or if he was the only member. [Baron Longshore](/wiki/Baron_Longshore) states that he was once a legitimate baron of Gilneas; though where his lands would have been, or if someone else was given jurisdiction over them, is unknown.

The [dog](/wiki/Mastiff) [Woofington](/wiki/Lord_Woofington) was given the title of lord of [Havenswood](/wiki/Havenswood) after the rest of the denizens of the island succumbed to madness.

## Trivia[]

- Gilneas appears to use nobility conventions of the United Kingdom, which is fitting given their inspiration from England.
  - The title of "Lord Mayor" is an actual title used in the United Kingdom, which is granted to the mayors of major cities.
  - [Lord Geoffery Tulvan](/wiki/Lord_Geoffery_Tulvan) is referred to as the "Earl of Evisceration".[10] Earl is a title only used within the United Kingdom and is the counterpart to the more commonly seen "Count", used by other countries.
  - The title used by [Alys Finnsson](/wiki/Dame_Alys_Finnsson), a Gilnean member of the [Twilight's Hammer](/wiki/Twilight%27s_Hammer), of Dame is a part of the British honors system, as a female counterpart to the honorific of 'sir' bestowed upon knights.

# Greymane family

- *Were you looking for the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall)?*
The **Greymane** family (also known as the **Greymane clan**)[1] is the ruling line of the [kingdom of Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)). The family ruled from [Greymane Manor](/wiki/Greymane_Manor) and had a Royal Chemist in the form of [Krennan Aranas](/wiki/Krennan_Aranas).

## Known members[]

- [King Archibald Greymane](/wiki/Archibald_Greymane) - father of Genn and former king of Gilneas.
  - [King Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) (and [Queen Mia Greymane](/wiki/Mia_Greymane)) - Ruler of the human and worgen of Gilneas, affected by the [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) curse himself. Mia is the wife of Genn and mother of Tess and Liam.[2]
    - [Prince Liam Greymane](/wiki/Liam_Greymane) - son of Genn Greymane. Died during the [Battle for Gilneas City](/wiki/The_Battle_for_Gilneas_City).
    - [Princess Tess Greymane](/wiki/Tess_Greymane), daughter of Genn Greymane.[3]

## Trivia[]

- *[Tides of Darkness](/wiki/Tides_of_Darkness)* spells the name as "Graymane".
- There are also an unrelated [Crispin Greymane](/wiki/Crispin_Greymane) dwarf and an [Elder Graymane](/wiki/Elder_Graymane) taunka.

“A kingdom is not a place, but a people.”

- — Mia Greymane, Queen of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas)

**Mia Greymane** is the wife of [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) and former queen consort of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)).

##
History

Mia met her future husband Genn at the Royal Aderic Banquet, where he was smitten by her. They later married for love, rather than political reasons.[1][2]

### Curse of the Worgen

**This section concerns content related to the *Warcraft* [manga](/wiki/Manga) or [comics](/wiki/Comics).**

Three days before the [worgen attack](/wiki/All_Hell_Breaks_Loose) on [Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City), Mia learned about the apparent death of [Halford Ramsey](/wiki/Halford_Ramsey) from his colleague [Cox](/wiki/Cox). Later, during a dinner she scolds her husband for spending too much time in his observatory (where he meets with [Belysra Starbreeze](/wiki/Belysra_Starbreeze), unbeknownst to his wife), neglecting his own family instead, especially Liam, who looks at him as an example. Later on, she witnesses the quarrel between Genn and [Vincent Godfrey](/wiki/Vincent_Godfrey) about the release of [Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley).

She is finally seen while calming down the [Duskhaven](/wiki/Duskhaven) refugees at [Greymane Manor](/wiki/Greymane_Manor).[3]

### Cataclysm

**This section concerns content related to *[Cataclysm](/wiki/World_of_Warcraft:_Cataclysm)*.**

She oversaw the evacuation of her people after the [Cataclysm](/wiki/Cataclysm_(event)) struck and the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) attacked her nation.[4]

At some point after [Duskhaven](/wiki/Duskhaven) is evacuated, Mia points players toward Genn Greymane to evacuate [Greymane Manor](/wiki/Greymane_Manor) in carriages. She notes that he is often stubborn.

#### Lord of His Pack

During the exodus to [Darnassus](/wiki/Darnassus), Mia and her daughter were aboard the *[Elune's Radiance](/wiki/Elune%27s_Radiance)* while Genn was on another ship. The fleet was hit by a powerful storm generated by the Cataclysm, and the *Elune's Radiance* started to sink. Having a leg broken during the storm, Mia could not move and [Tess](/wiki/Tess) remained with her refusing to leave, so they both risked drowning. Genn, refusing to lose the last two members of his family, assumed [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) form and joined the rescue efforts of the night elf sailors from his ship. He reached their room inside the ship and brought them out, carrying Mia in his arms and Tess on his back, then he dropped them into the sea, where they were reached by the night elves lifeboats. Mia's broken leg was healed by the [druids](/wiki/Druid), and after the storm, both the women reached [Teldrassil](/wiki/Teldrassil) safely.[5]

### Battle for Azeroth

During the [War of the Thorns](/wiki/War_of_the_Thorns), the [Alliance](/wiki/Alliance) was busy evacuating refugees from [Ashenvale](/wiki/Ashenvale_Forest) and [Darnassus](/wiki/Darnassus) to [Stormwind City](/wiki/Stormwind_City). With King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane) preoccupied with advising King [Anduin Wrynn](/wiki/Anduin_Wrynn) for the upcoming war, a respected authority figure was needed to calm the Gilnean people at the [Howling Oak](/wiki/Howling_Oak) and organize their evacuation to [Stormwind City](/wiki/Stormwind_City). Queen Mia was the most suitable person available and was eager to fulfill the role when Genn asked her to, especially after [Tess Greymane](/wiki/Tess_Greymane) was nowhere to be found. It was mentioned that Anduin admired her quick wits and kind heart, and that while Mia lived in Stormwind with her husband, she spent half her time in Darnassus to support her people settled there, and was a frequent visitor to their encampment, having also formed a close friendship with [Astarii Starseeker](/wiki/Astarii_Starseeker), one of the [Priestesses of the Moon](/wiki/Priestesses_of_the_Moon).

Mia asked [Maelir](/wiki/Maelir), one of the [Highborne](/wiki/Highborne), to help evacuate her people from Darnassus, to which he agreed, replying that it was his honor to assist the Gilneans. After most of her people were successfully evacuated from the city, Mia, having developed a deep love for the people of Darnassus, was determined to aid in the night elven evacuation as well, acting as the ambassador of Stormwind, and she remained until the [Burning of Teldrassil](/wiki/Burning_of_Teldrassil) and still attempting to aid the priestesses at the [Temple of the Moon](/wiki/Temple_of_the_Moon) - despite Genn's urging her repeatedly to leave Teldrassil before it was too late. Although she realized that it was impossible to evacuate their entire population, Mia vowed to Astarii that Genn would lead those who came to reclaim the World Tree from the Horde afterwards. After Tyrande Whisperwind returned to help Malfurion Stormrage, believing that defeating Sylvanas would disorganize the Horde and perhaps give her people more time to evacuate, Mia told the night elves to honor their high priestess as she joined her husband in battle against the Horde.

When Sylvanas and the Horde launched their final assault on Teldrassil, Mia still refused to leave and attempted to help organize the remaining night elves scrambling to enter a portal, despite Astarii's insistence that she return to her husband. Mia was seriously wounded trying to protect [Finel](/wiki/Finel), a night elven infant, from collapsing rubble within the Temple, which trapped her beneath their debris and broke her legs. After Genn arrived to rescue her, Astarii managed to heal her wounds. Although Mia told Genn to take Finel and leave her, Genn stubbornly refused, and managed to rescue both of them, bringing them to Stormwind.[6][7] With the World Tree and their second home destroyed, the surviving Gilneans moved to Stormwind, where Mia helped priests tend to the injured Gilnean and night elven refugees in the [Cathedral of Light](/wiki/Cathedral_of_Light).

After Anduin was unable to directly provide assistance for Tyrande Whisperwind and at her people, Genn mentioned that Mia would likely charge off to battle without him if he did not assist the night elves. Although the Queen of Gilneas did not join the [Battle for Darkshore](/wiki/Battle_for_Darkshore) herself, her daughter Tess and many of her people subsequently traveled to [Darkshore](/wiki/Darkshore), openly aiding the kaldorei forces fighting against the Horde.[8]

### Shadowlands

Ater the end of the [Fourth War](/wiki/Fourth_War), Mia was present in [Bashal'Aran](/wiki/Bashal%27Aran) and witnessed Tyrande's speech about Horde's defeat in [Darkshore](/wiki/Darkshore).[9]

### The Vow Eternal

A few years later, after Genn received an invitation to the wedding of [Lor'themar Theron](/wiki/Lor%27themar_Theron) and [Thalyssra](/wiki/Thalyssra), and refused to attend it, Mia elected to go in his stead. During the reception, she spoke with [Alleria Windrunner](/wiki/Alleria_Windrunner), and the queen whispered something that made bursted into laughter the elven ranger. During the party, the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) delegation consisting of [Derek Proudmoore](/wiki/Derek_Proudmoore), [Calia Menethil](/wiki/Calia_Menethil), and [Lilian Voss](/wiki/Lilian_Voss) were uncomfortable at Genn's rejection but Calia noted that it was a pleasure to see the queen again.[10]

  - It is worth noting that while [Katherine Proudmoore](/wiki/Katherine_Proudmoore), wife of [Daelin Proudmoore](/wiki/Daelin_Proudmoore) the former leader of Kul Tiras, was referred to as a queen in the beta for Battle for Azeroth and her family's role echoes that of monarchy, Kul Tiras does not use the title of queen or king and any reference of a queen was removed from the game before the expansion went live, thus leaving Mia as the only living human queen.
- In Stormwind City, while helping the [Wounded Refugees](/wiki/Wounded_Refugee), she is seen at 80% of health.
- Mia is voiced by [Tara Fitzgerald](/wiki/Tara_Fitzgerald) in *[Battle for Azeroth](/wiki/World_of_Warcraft:_Battle_for_Azeroth)*.[11]

Prince **Liam Greymane** was a member of the royal family of [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_(kingdom)), and the son and heir of King [Genn Greymane](/wiki/Genn_Greymane).[1] He was killed by [Sylvanas Windrunner](/wiki/Sylvanas_Windrunner) during the [Battle for](/wiki/Invasion_of_Gilneas#Battle_of_Gilneas_City)[Gilneas City](/wiki/Gilneas_City).

## Biography[]

### Lord of His Pack[]

As a teenager, Liam often disagreed with his father and had quarrels with him, particularly over seceding from the [Alliance](/wiki/Alliance_of_Lordaeron) and constructing the [Greymane Wall](/wiki/Greymane_Wall). When the [Plague of Undeath](/wiki/Plague_of_Undeath) began to overtake [Lordaeron](/wiki/Lordaeron_(kingdom)), causing the nation to plead for aid from Gilneas, Liam rebuked his father for not sending any help to their fellow kingdom. A slightly drunken Genn — furious that his own son would question him — threw his goblet of wine across the floor, insisted that the wall would protect Gilneas from the undead, and stated that he would not risk the lives of any Gilneans by sending them to fight the [Scourge](/wiki/Scourge), just as his [own father](/wiki/Archibald_Greymane) wouldn't have. Liam accused Genn of always trying to emulate his father and that there were other ways to consider, but Genn replied that it was a prince's duty to strive to be like his father. Liam retorted that he thought it was a prince's duty to one day be a great king. The prince then took his leave, knowing that the argument was lost.

After the [Third War](/wiki/Third_War) began, Liam watched alongside Genn, Archmage [Arugal](/wiki/Arugal), and a guard captain from atop the Greymane Wall as a massive sea of the Scourge assaulted it in waves. Liam told his father that he should have listened to him. Genn — angered that his son would question him again, this time in public while he was trying to instill courage in the wall's defenders — brusquely told his son that now was not the time.

### The Fall of Gilneas[]

**This section concerns content related to the *Warcraft*[manga](/wiki/Manga) or [comics](/wiki/Comics).**

The Fall of Gilneas[]
| | This section is **a [lore](/wiki/Lore) stub**. |
|---|---|
**This section concerns content related to *[Cataclysm](/wiki/World_of_Warcraft:_Cataclysm)*.**

Years later, when the invading [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) began to beset the Greymane Wall, Liam was ordered by his father to oversee the defenses of the wall. Yet with the swelling ranks of the Forsaken and the recent [worgen](/wiki/Worgen) invasion of Gilneas City, he was presumably forced to abandon his post and was ordered to secure [Merchant Square](/wiki/Merchant_Square), which he helped defend with the aid of a Gilnean [adventurer](/wiki/Adventurer). After the squares were lost to the worgen, Liam met with his father and the former rebel [Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley) in the [Greymane Court](/wiki/Greymane_Court). Darius told Genn that some would have to remain behind to distract the worgen in order to allow the rest of the Gilneans to evacuate from the city. Liam wished to stay behind with the [Royal Guard](/wiki/Gilnean_Royal_Guard) and protect the city, but Crowley retorted that it would be better for Liam to accompany Genn, since they couldn't afford to have the king wondering if his son was alive or not.

Shortly after Darius decided to stay behind in [Light's Dawn Cathedral](/wiki/Light%27s_Dawn_Cathedral) and make a last stand against the worgen, Darius' daughter [Lorna Crowley](/wiki/Lorna_Crowley) met with Genn and Liam. She had received word that her father was free, but Liam told her about the choice Darius made. Lorna pulled out her gun and took aim at Genn, cursing at him and believing this was his idea of revenge after the [Northgate Rebellion](/wiki/Northgate_Rebellion). Liam restrained her, and a hysterical Lorna demanded she be let go to die with her father before she began to cry in Liam's arms.

Liam and his father escaped with the other Gilnean refugees to the village of [Duskhaven](/wiki/Duskhaven). With all that had transpired, Gilneas was now faced with a terrible truth: their mighty wall could not hold back the dead much longer. Despite all that happened, Liam still believed in his father, despite Genn's doubts. Liam believed Genn could be a great leader once again if he could only regain his confidence in himself. Liam later observed the effects of [Krennan Aranas](/wiki/Krennan_Aranas)' elixir on the worgen.

Liam started drinking to drown his regrets of being unable to prevent the loss of Gilneas City, but when the [Forsaken](/wiki/Forsaken) attacked [Gilneas](/wiki/Gilneas_peninsula), he and his men fought back. Liam was overjoyed to reunite the adventurer from Gilneas City, even though the hero had now been transformed into a worgen. While Liam was heading towards the main Forsaken army, the [Cataclysm](/wiki/Cataclysm_(event)) occurred and drowned the land near Duskhaven. Liam assisted in rescuing drowning Gilnean soldiers and helped evacuate the village. He then traveled to [Stormglen](/wiki/Stormglen_Village) with the other evacuees, but along the way his stagecoach was attacked by [ogres](/wiki/Ogre). With the help of the adventurer, Liam rescued crash survivors from the [nearby marsh](/wiki/Hailwood_Marsh) and dealt with the ogres by tricking their leader, the [ettin](/wiki/Ettin)[Koroth the Hillbreaker](/wiki/Koroth_the_Hillbreaker), into attacking the Forsaken.

Some days later, Genn told his son the truth about how the curse spread and revealed to him that he was bitten. Liam was fine with the revelations, leading to a reconciliation between him and his father.

After the Gilneans united due to the efforts of his father and [Darius Crowley](/wiki/Darius_Crowley), Liam sobered up and prepared to lead a counter attack against the Forsaken invaders. After holding a passionate speech, he lead his men in the [Battle of Gilneas City](/wiki/The_Battle_for_Gilneas_City), helping to reclaim the city's districts before meeting up with his father and Lord Crowley to confront the Forsaken's leader, [Sylvanas Windrunner](/wiki/Sylvanas_Windrunner). During the ensuing battle, Liam was killed by Sylvanas when he took a poisoned arrow intended for Genn. He died in his father's arms, secure in the knowledge that the city had been retaken. After the battle, the Gilneans learned that Sylvanas was planning to loose the [New Plague](/wiki/New_Plague) on Gilneas, leaving Genn with the choice of pursuing vengeance by striking at the Banshee Queen or evacuating his people. As much as he wished to exact vengeance, the king felt he had to honor his son's memory and thus traveled to the holy burial ground of [Aderic's Repose](/wiki/Aderic%27s_Repose) along with Krennan, Darius, and Lorna. There, they laid Liam to rest alongside other patriots and heroes of Gilneas.

- [![Prince Liam on horseback.](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowpedia/images/5/5e/Prince_Liam_Greymane_on_horseback_in_Gilneas_City.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/49?cb=20151102151548)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/wowpedia/images/5/5e/Prince_Liam_Greymane_on_horseback_in_Gilneas_City.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20151102151548)

Liam after the evacuation from Duskhaven.

### Legacy[]

After Liam's death, Genn continued to be haunted by the memory of his son, particularly the quarrels they had and the sight of the prince's dying body after the Battle of Gilneas City. During the exodus to [Darnassus](/wiki/Darnassus), Genn nearly drowned while saving his [remaining](/wiki/Mia_Greymane)[family](/wiki/Tess_Greymane) from the sinking *[Elune's Radiance](/wiki/Elune%27s_Radiance)*, but was saved by the [night elf](/wiki/Night_elf) captain [Talar Oaktalon](/wiki/Talar_Oaktalon). After later awakening, Genn told Talar that he had been dreaming of Liam and that while there would be times when his child's death would hit him like a stone thrown at his chest, he could take comfort and pride in knowing that his son had been a wiser man than him.[2]

In [Stormheim](/wiki/Stormheim), Genn stole the magical [Soulcage](/wiki/Soulcage) from Sylvanas to prevent her from enslaving [Eyir](/wiki/Eyir) and destroyed it, referencing Liam's death by saying "You took my son's future, and now I've taken yours".[3]

In *[Battle for Azeroth](/wiki/Battle_for_Azeroth)*, Genn makes reference to avenging Liam when the Gilnean forces are sent to flank [Orgrimmar](/wiki/Orgrimmar) during [Varok Saurfang](/wiki/Varok_Saurfang)'s rebellion. He ultimately is outraged to find Sylvanas has escaped yet again, denying him justice. Liam's death is relived by his sister, [Tess Greymane](/wiki/Tess_Greymane), during the worgen heritage armor questline. In a vision granted to her by [Goldrinn](/wiki/Goldrinn), of what she could have changed as a worgen, Tess is unable to prevent her brother's death, leading to her falling into an enraged state before being defeated and calmed by the worgen hero assisting her. She forlornly realizes that she couldn't have saved Liam either, before coming to terms with her reasons for seeking out the Curse.[[*citation needed*]](/wiki/Wowpedia:Citation)

## Trivia[]

- The speech made by Liam before the battle in Gilneas City is reminiscent of [Winston Churchill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Winston_Churchill)'s speech in the House of Commons on June 4, 1940, during the Battle of Britain. Faced with overwhelming odds, Churchill vowed that *"we shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; we shall never surrender"*.
- He wielded a [[Rough Boomstick]](/wiki/Rough_Boomstick) during the *[Cataclysm](/wiki/World_of_Warcraft:_Cataclysm)* beta, but wields a normal Gilnean rifle in the live version of the game.
- Liam is voiced by [Zach Appelman](/wiki/Zach_Appelman).
- Liam's ghost appears as [a legendary card](https://hearthstone.fandom.com/wiki/Prince_Liam) for the paladin class in the *[The Witchwood](/wiki/Hearthstone:_The_Witchwood)* expansion for *[Hearthstone](/wiki/Hearthstone_(game))*. His flavor text reads: *"I have a very particular set of skills. Skills that make me a nightmare for witches like you."* In *Hearthstone* lore, Liam's spirit is rumored to appear and help people in great danger, perhaps because he failed Gilneas once before and a desire to do better fetters him to the mortal plane, or perhaps because the curse of the Witchwood denies him eternal rest. Whatever the case, this version of Liam is not done serving Gilneas.[4]

Queen Tess Greymane is a member of the Royal Family of Gilneas, the daughter of King Genn Greymane.[2] Following to her brother's death, Tess became heir to the throne of the kingdom of Gilneas.[3] With Liam gone, Tess is searching for answers to questions she never thought she would ask.[4] After the successful reclamation of their kingdom, Genn bestowed the throne to Tess, officially becoming the Queen of Gilneas.

## History

### Childhood

Tess' life was saved by a potion made by Krennan Aranas; if not for him, she would have died soon after she was born.[2] When she was a little girl, her father told her that she was to find one beautiful thing every day and that it would make the hard days easier.[5]

### Curse of the Worgen

This section concerns content related to the Warcraft manga or comics.

Tess in Curse of the Worgen.

After the Cataclysm destroyed the town of Duskhaven, Tess ventured up to her father's observatory with a single peacebloom flower. She reminded Genn the words he would tell Tess as a girl. Even among the ruined Gilneas, she was able to find an unharmed peacebloom, and it gave her hope.

### Lord of His Pack

This section concerns content related to the Warcraft novels, novellas, or short stories.

During the exodus to Darnassus, Tess and her mother, Mia Greymane, were aboard the Elune's Radiance while her father was on another ship. The fleet was hit by a powerful storm generated by the Cataclysm, and the ship started to sink. Having a leg broken during the storm, Mia could not move and Tess remained with her refusing to leave, so they both risked to drown. Genn, refusing to lose the last two members of his family, assumed the worgen form and joined the rescue efforts of the night elf sailors from his ship. After the storm, both the women reached Teldrassil safely.[6] Tess' whereabouts until Legion were unknown, but it is possible that she followed her father to Stormwind City.

### Legion

This section concerns content related to Legion.

Darius and Tess present for the award ceremony of the player character in Legion.

In the aftermath of the Battle for the Broken Shore, Tess appears on the Skyfire that brings adventurers and other wounded back to Stormwind. If the player chooses to take the optional offered Gryphon ride to Stormwind Keep, she and Lorna Crowley will escort them on their own gryphons, conversing on the way. When flying to Stormwind Keep, Princess Tess Greymane confided to Lorna her concern about the lust for vengeance consuming her father. Lorna states that all Gilneans suffer from that rage, her father more than most. Though Tess concurs with Lorna, she fears more deaths are sure to come. Lorna Crowley is the daughter of Lord Darius Crowley, one of the principal leaders during the Northgate Rebellion. After the retaking of Gilneas City, she joined her father as commander of the Gilneas Liberation Front. When the Burning Legion returned to assault Azeroth, Lorna and Darius joined Genn Greymane on the Skyfire as part of his army forces.

## Background

### Fall of Gilneas

This section concerns content related to the Warcraft manga or comics.

This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.

Lorna Crowley in Gilneas.

Lorna during Exodus.

The day of the worgen attack on Gilneas City, Lorna saved a worgen adventurer by shooting Josiah Avery. The two of them worked together to get the Northgate rebels' hidden arsenal for Greymane's army.

Shortly after, she met with King Genn and Prince Liam after her father chose to stay behind in the Light's Dawn Cathedral and make a last stand against the worgen. She had received word her father was free, but Liam told her about the choice Darius made. Lorna pulled out her gun and took aim at Genn, cursing at him and believing this was his idea of revenge after the Northgate Rebellion. Liam restrained her, and a hysterical Lorna demanded she be let go to die with her father before she began to cry in Liam's arms. Afterward she returned to the Crowley Orchard and lived as a hermit. Before being evacuated, she and the worgen adventurer worked together to rescue some horses. She then moved to the Greymane Manor and from there she took a carriage with Gwen Armstead to Stormglen where she found a diary of Bradshaw and learned that the man ventured into Blackwald. She sent him there only to find the night elf Belysra Starbreeze along with other worgen. Darius was revealed to have had survived and become a worgen. He was worried how Lorna would respond to his curse, but she was fine with it.

She was then sent to Livery Outpost to rescue the villagers from northern Gilneas and free Emberstone Village. Lorna then aided the Worgen adventurers in retaking Gilneas City after the first assault of the Forsaken. After the death of Liam, she learned that the Forsaken were going to use the plague on the city. She was present at Liam's funeral in Aderic's Repose. After that she moved to Keel Harbor and loaded explosives onto an Orc Gunship and used it as a ram to destroy the Forsaken forward camp next to the Greymane Wall.

### Gilneas Liberation Front

Following the invasion of Gilneas, Lorna joined her father as commander of the Gilneas Liberation Front and fought with the Alliance to retake the Ruins of Gilneas from the Forsaken. She attacked the Forsaken Forward Command as she used [Forsaken Communication Device] to declare that the Alliance once agai
